title: Injection sequence
purpose: Inspect a version of the actual recorded instrument injection order for an analytical batch.
summary: Inspect a recorded instrument run, find the verifications around a sample, and compare sample injection counts with the maximum in your method or SOP. You can open any version of the sequence.

tasks.title: Find verification positions around a sample
steps: Find the sample injection by [[Position]] or [[Instrument label]].
Read [[Verification before]] and [[Verification after]] for the nearest recorded position and label on each side.

tasks.title: Check sample counts between verifications
steps: Select [[Verification intervals]] under [[On this page]] to see the counts for this version.
Enter the maximum from your method or SOP in [[Maximum sample injections]] and select [[Compare counts]].
Read [[Count comparison]] with the earlier and later verification positions. Check any missing verification against the source record.

tasks.title: Trace a correction
steps: In [[Version history]], check who recorded the correction, when and why.
Select a version link to read that sequence. If you opened an earlier version, select [[Go to current version]] to return to the latest.

tasks.title: Correct the recorded order
steps: From the [[Current version]], select [[Correct injection sequence]].
Check the prefilled sequence against the source record, make the correction and give a reason.

good_to_know: [[None recorded]] means there is no verification on that side of the sample in this version.
Use your method and lab SOP to judge which verification applies, how often it is required and whether it is acceptable.
Repeated injections of the same sample each count once. Standards, blanks and other injections stay visible in [[Injections]] and contribute zero to the count.
Only the latest version can be corrected. Every earlier version retains its own source reference, rows and authorship.
Instrument labels come from the source transcription. Identify the sample using that record when the same label appears more than once.

items.label: Run reference / Version / Batch
items.description: The heading is the fixed instrument run identifier. The version number identifies the exact transcription shown. Select the batch number to return to the analytical batch.

items.label: Current version / Superseded
items.description: Current version identifies the latest sequence. Superseded identifies an earlier version saved before a correction. Go to current version leads from an earlier transcription to the latest one.

items.label: Source reference
items.description: Identifier of the instrument record used for the version you are viewing.

items.label: Recorded by / Recorded at
items.description: Staff member who saved the version and the date and time in the laboratory’s time zone.

items.label: Reason for correction
items.description: The explanation saved when this version corrected the previous one. Version 1 has no correction reason.

items.label: On this page
items.description: Jump to Sequence details, Verification intervals, Injections or Version history for the open version.

items.label: Earlier verification / Later verification
items.description: The position and instrument label of each verification bordering an interval. No earlier verification or No later verification identifies an open end. With no recorded verifications, one row covers the whole run.

items.label: Sample injections
items.description: Count of positions marked Sample in that interval, including repeated injections. Consecutive verifications have a count of zero. Rows before the first or after the last verification appear whenever those parts of the sequence contain injections of any kind.

items.label: Maximum sample injections / Compare counts
items.description: Optional positive whole number. Enter the maximum your method or SOP uses for sample injections and select Compare counts. An invalid entry stays in the field with an error. The recorded counts are still shown.

items.label: Count comparison
items.description: Over maximum means the interval contains more sample injections than you entered. At or below maximum includes an exact match. Both apply only to counts, including at open ends. Review the source, analyte, verification results and your method to decide whether the checks apply and are acceptable.

items.label: Clear comparison
items.description: Return to the counts alone on the same version. The maximum applies to this view and changes no sequence, QC record or release decision.

items.label: No intervals to compare
items.description: A single verification with no other injections has no interval. You can inspect its position and label in Injections.

items.label: Position
items.description: The recorded injection position, starting at 1. The table shows every injection in position order.

items.label: Kind
items.description: The recorded type of this injection: Sample, Verification, Standard, Blank or Other.

items.label: Instrument label
items.description: The label transcribed from the source at that position. Duplicate labels can occur at different positions.

items.label: Verification before / Verification after
items.description: For each Sample, the nearest Verification on each side of it in this version, shown as position and label. The table can show a gap on one or both sides. Other injection kinds show a dash in both columns.

sections.title: Version history and actions

items.label: Version history
items.description: Shows the first recording and all corrections for this run, oldest first, with each save’s actor, time and any correction reason. Select a numbered version link to open its recorded sequence.

items.label: Correct injection sequence
items.description: Analysts and administrators can open a form to create the next version with a reason. The action is disabled on superseded versions, where Go to current version leads to the latest.

paragraphs: Staff with an application role can read every version. Client accounts cannot access the record. Use the batch’s result and QC workflows for analytical and release decisions.
